transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you—what has been bothering you lately, and what brought you in to see me today?

I feel like I can’t think straight anymore or make simple decisions at work or school, and it’s really starting to scare me. My mind feels foggy all the time, and things that used to be automatic now take me forever, like I’m constantly second‑guessing myself.

Do you ever have sudden episodes where, out of the blue, you feel an intense surge of fear or discomfort with physical symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, chest tightness, or feeling like you might lose control or die, that peak within minutes?
No, I don’t really get sudden panic attacks like that. My anxiety feels more like a constant background thing tied to stress and overthinking, not big intense waves that come out of nowhere.

Over the past couple of weeks, have you mostly been feeling down or depressed nearly every day, or is it more that you feel constantly tense and worried about many things even if your mood isn’t especially low?

It’s more that I’ve been feeling down and depressed pretty much every day. I do worry about things, but the main thing is this heavy, gray, sad feeling that’s just there most of the time, even when nothing specific is going wrong.
In addition to feeling down, have you noticed that activities you used to enjoy now feel less interesting or less pleasurable, and if so, how much has that changed for you?

Yeah, that’s definitely been happening. I used to really look forward to my evening runs, knitting, and hanging out with friends, but now I mostly just lie in bed scrolling on my phone, ignore messages, and feel pretty much nothing when I think about doing those things. It’s been that way for months, not just once in a while.
How long have you been feeling this depressed and uninterested in things most days in a row—has it been at least two weeks straight, and if so, about how many months has this been going on like this?

Yeah, it’s definitely been at least two weeks straight—more like many months in a row. Looking back, it really started around when I began working full-time at the clinic and started my nursing classes, so it’s been a little over a year now of feeling this way most days.

Before this past year, have you ever had other periods lasting at least a couple of weeks where you felt similarly depressed and uninterested in things, with a clear return to your usual self in between, or is this the first time in your life it’s been like this?

This is the first time it’s been like this and lasted this long. I’ve had normal stress or feeling down for a few days before, but nothing that stuck around for weeks and months like this with no real break.
Over the past couple of weeks, how have your sleep and appetite been—are you sleeping or eating much more or much less than usual, and has that been happening nearly every day?

My appetite’s been really low most days—I’ll go through a whole shift on just coffee, then realize at night I never ate a real meal, and my scrubs are starting to feel loose. Sleep has been rough too: I lie awake for hours with my mind racing about mistakes, don’t fall asleep until really late, wake up a lot, and get up feeling like I barely slept.
With how low you’ve been feeling, have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, that you’d be better off dead, or any thoughts about hurting or killing yourself?

Yeah… on my worst nights I do catch myself thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up, or that I’m so behind it doesn’t matter anymore. I haven’t made any plans or tried to hurt myself, and the idea of actually doing something scares me, plus I still worry about my family and school, which kind of keeps me from going further with those thoughts.

Besides the low mood and poor sleep, have you noticed feeling physically slowed down or restless, or that your thinking and concentration are clearly worse than before, and if so, how much is that affecting your ability to function at work or in school?

Yeah, I feel both physically slowed down and mentally foggy most days. My coworkers say I move in slow motion, and even simple things like walking the hall or starting my charting feel like I’m dragging myself, and it takes me forever to write notes or focus on quizzes. It’s bad enough that I’ve fallen behind in my coursework and even got written up at the clinic for charting errors.

Have you ever had a period lasting several days when your mood was unusually high or irritable, you needed much less sleep, had a lot more energy than usual, or felt so driven and confident that others thought you were acting unlike your usual self?
No, I’ve never really had a stretch like that. I don’t remember any time where I was extra energized or needed way less sleep and felt unusually high or wired for days.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has had over a year of nearly daily depressed mood, marked loss of interest, insomnia, decreased appetite with weight loss, psychomotor retardation, impaired concentration/indecisiveness, and recurrent passive thoughts of death, causing significant functional impairment at work and in school. There is no history of manic or hypomanic episodes, and the current symptom severity clearly exceeds mild, fitting a single current moderate depressive episode (F32.1). Generalized anxiety disorder is less likely because the core and most impairing features are depressive, and the worry is secondary; mild depression (F32.0) is less consistent with the degree of impairment and symptom load.
